explanation_profile.concept: Grammar atoms as structural contracts for catalog atom classes

body.inline:
## What is a grammar atom?

A *grammar atom* is a special atom type in schema-atoms that defines the structural contract for a catalog's primary atom class. Where a JSON Schema atom specifies the machine-readable validation rules, a grammar atom provides the human-readable narrative: what fields exist, why they exist, what the invariants are, and how the schema is expected to evolve.

## Why they exist

The *-atoms ecosystem has 25+ catalogs, each with its own primary atom type. Without grammar atoms, the structural contracts for each type would be scattered across READMEs, ADRs, and comments inside JSON Schema files — discoverable only if you know where to look. Grammar atoms make the contracts first-class citizens of the ecosystem: indexable, linkable, and evolvable through the same PR-and-release process as any other atom.

## Anatomy of a grammar atom

A grammar atom in schema-atoms looks like this:

```json
{
  "schema": "https://schema-atoms.com/schemas/atom-v1.json",
  "type": "grammar",
  "id": "doc-atoms-v1",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "name": "doc-atoms v1 atom grammar",
  "summary": "Structural contract for doc-atoms primary atom class.",
  "body": {
    "format": "markdown",
    "inline": "## Required fields\n..."
  }
}
```

The `id` follows the convention `<catalog>-v<major>` to make versioning explicit at a glance.

## Grammar atoms vs JSON Schema atoms

| | Grammar atom | JSON Schema atom |
|---|---|---|
| Format | JSON (body is Markdown) | JSON (body references a `.json` schema file) |
| Purpose | Human-readable narrative contract | Machine-readable validation rules |
| Consumer | Contributors, reviewers, AI tooling | Validators, CI, code generators |
| Evolution | Prose amendments, new sections | Additive schema changes with version bump |

## Relationship to catalogs

Each catalog's grammar atom lives in schema-atoms, not in the catalog itself. This separation keeps schema-atoms as the single authoritative registry of structural contracts while keeping catalog repos focused on their own atom content. A catalog's CI pipeline references its grammar atom ID when running the validator.
